Guide / Updated November 2026

Is hipages worth it? The real cost per job.

hipages can be worth it for a new business in a big city that needs jobs on the calendar and can call every lead straight back. For most established trades it is an expensive way to win small jobs, because each lead is shared with other tradies and the monthly plan runs whether the phone rings or not. Here is how to check your own numbers.

Is hipages worth it for tradies?

It depends on the size of your jobs and how fast you respond. hipages charges a monthly subscription for a set number of credits, and you spend those credits to contact homeowners who post a job. Several businesses can contact the same homeowner, so you are competing on speed and price from the first minute.

Tradies on forums describe it the same way again and again: useful to get off the ground, then dropped once referrals and Google reviews carry the business. The ones who stay tend to do larger jobs, where one win pays for months of credits.

How much does hipages cost in 2026?

hipages does not publish a dollar price per lead. What is publicly tracked and widely reported looks like this:

  • Plans: tracked monthly plans run from about $249 to $649 a month, plus GST, with higher tiers for bigger businesses.
  • Lead cost: independent estimates put a typical lead at roughly $25 to $80, depending on the trade, the job and the area.
  • Contract: plans are commonly sold on a 12 month term, so the renewal date matters as much as the price.
  • Sharing: each lead usually goes to more than one business, commonly reported as three to five.

What a hipages job really costs you

The useful number is not cost per lead, it is cost per won job:

Cost per won job = (monthly plan + any extra credits) ÷ jobs you actually won that month.

A simple example: a $249 plan buys roughly seven leads in a category priced at about 42 credits each. Win one in five and you book about 1.4 jobs, so each job costs you around $178 in platform fees alone. That is fine on a $6,000 bathroom. On a $250 call out it wipes out the profit.

The same sum at different spends and win rates (examples):

$24971 in 5about $178

Add the time spent driving out to quote jobs you never win, and the real figure is higher again.

When hipages is worth it

  • You are new, have no reviews yet and need work this month.
  • Your average job is large: renovations, installs, landscaping projects.
  • Someone can answer and call back within minutes, every day.
  • You use it to fill quiet weeks, not as your only source of work.

hipages alternatives that you own

The cheapest lead is the one that comes straight to you and nobody else. The same four things come up in every tradie forum:

  1. Google Business Profile. Free, and it puts you on Google Maps where locals search. Use our Google Business Profile checklist.
  2. Google reviews. Text a review link to every happy customer, including the ones who found you on hipages.
  3. Your own website. A fast site with a page for each service and suburb turns searches into calls only you receive. See what a trade website needs.
  4. Builders and repeat clients. Look after the builders, property managers and designers who can send steady work.

How to leave hipages without a gap in work

  • Find your contract end date and the cancellation terms before you do anything else.
  • Get your Google Business Profile and website working a few weeks before the plan ends.
  • Ask every customer you won through the platform for a Google review.
  • Ask every new caller how they found you, so you know what is working.

If you stay on hipages: how to win more of the jobs you pay for

  • Call, do not just message. The first business to have a real conversation usually wins. Call within minutes, and message only if they do not pick up.
  • Be picky about categories and areas. Turn off job types that rarely pay for themselves and postcodes too far to drive profitably.
  • Fill out your profile properly. Photos of real jobs, your licence details and a clear description make homeowners choose you from the list.
  • Quote fast. A clear written price the same day beats a better price three days later.
  • Turn every platform job into a Google review. That way each job you pay for keeps working for you after the platform is gone.

Where Australian homeowners actually look

In renovation forums, homeowners describe searching Google first, reading reviews, and looking for photos of past work before they call. Some say they struggle to find good trades at all because so many have no website or listing. That is why a complete Google Business Profile, a stack of recent reviews and a simple website with your real work on it put you in front of customers who never open a lead app. See how trades get found on Google Maps.

Quick answers

Common questions.

How much does hipages cost per month?

Publicly tracked plans run from about $249 to $649 a month plus GST, with credits included. Lead prices are not published and vary by trade and area.

How many tradies get the same hipages lead?

Usually more than one. Tradies and independent reviews commonly report three to five businesses contacting the same homeowner.

Can I cancel hipages anytime?

Plans are commonly sold on a 12 month term. Check your own agreement for the end date and cancellation terms before you sign or renew.

What is the best alternative to hipages?

Leads you own: a complete Google Business Profile, steady Google reviews, a fast website with service and suburb pages, and repeat work from builders and past clients.

Is hipages worth it for electricians or plumbers?

It can be for larger jobs like switchboard upgrades, solar or hot water installs. For small call outs the platform fee often costs more than the job makes.
